me.name: Chris Chen
me.bio:
CS student at the University of Toronto, St. George, Class of 2030.

I build things people actually use. Right now that's Inkference, the app you're on: portfolios, live chat, planners, and communities, all built and shipped by me.

Before that, I spent my high school years on FTC robotics. With Pluto we placed #2 in Ontario and went to the 2024 World Championship. With Hydra, a custom CNC robot, we competed at FTC's first New England Premier event. I did CAD, 3D printing and the code, from autonomous paths to vision with OpenCV.

Off the keyboard: skateboarding, guitar and art.

Building something cool? Send me a message. 

Also looking to intern at a cool company for summer 2027!

projects.title: Noutes V2
projects.summary: Noutes V2 is a TypeScript social app using React, Appwrite, and Tailwind. Features include auth, dynamic posts, responsive UI, and form validation.
projects.description:
Noutes Social Media App V2 is a fully responsive, modern web application built using ReactJS, TypeScript, and Vite. It leverages a powerful tech stack including Appwrite for backend services, TailwindCSS and Shadcn for sleek UI components, and Zod for form validation. The app features a clean and dynamic user interface, allowing users to create accounts, log in, and interact with content in real time.

The primary goal of this version was to improve upon the original Noutes app by implementing scalable and maintainable code using modern web development practices. With the integration of TanStack for data fetching and caching, the app ensures smooth performance and real-time updates. Users can create and manage posts, while components are structured with reusable logic and optimized state management using React hooks like useState and useEffect.

Deployed via Vercel for global performance, Noutes V2 also demonstrates strong design practices with mobile-first responsiveness and lazy-loaded media. This version lays the groundwork for future enhancements such as messaging, comments, and notification systems, while serving as a demonstration of full-stack app design using modern tools.

projects.title: Noutes (Final Product)
projects.summary: A social app with styled posts (Noutes), real-time chat, explore feed, infinite scroll, profile editing, and secure auth with email verification.
projects.description:
Noutes is a full-stack social platform I built with a focus on real-time interaction, user expression, and seamless UX. The app features secure email authentication with full support for verification, password reset, and account recovery. Users can personalize their profiles by updating their name, username, email, bio, birthdate, and password. Each profile includes rich social features such as following, friending, and profile browsing.

At the core of the platform are Noutes—customizable post-like entries that support images and styled text via HTML parsing. Each Noute supports descriptions, liking, saving, and visibility across user feeds. The Explore page allows users to search both profiles and Noutes, while highlighting the most viewed and most liked content. Both the home feed and Explore feed implement infinite scrolling powered by TanStack Query for smooth, efficient data loading.

To support real-time communication, I integrated Socket.IO for instant messaging between friends. Combined with thoughtful UI/UX, scalable architecture, and robust authentication, Noutes delivers a dynamic and personalized social experience.

I also made this app a Progressive Web App (PWA), allowing it to run full screen and provide users with a more immersive experience.

projects.title: Pluto
projects.summary: Built and programmed FTC robot PLUTO; placed #2 in Ontario and competed at 2024 Worlds. Focused on design, code, and autonomous systems.
projects.description: In my first year with the FIRST Tech Challenge team 19498 Devolotics, I served as both a builder and programmer for our competitive robot, PLUTO. Over a 10-month season, we designed, built, and coded a robot for the Centerstage challenge. PLUTO featured a mecanum drivetrain for omnidirectional movement, angled linear slides, a surgical tubing intake, and a pixel storage/deposit system with two degrees of motion. We also engineered a drone (paper airplane) launcher and a hanging mechanism. On the software side, I helped develop an autonomous program using Java, TensorFlow, and OpenCV, enabling the robot to detect team props, navigate the field, and score points without driver input. Our efforts led to a #2 ranking in Ontario and qualification for the 2024 World Championships in Houston, Texas. I also contributed to CAD design using Onshape, subsystem optimization, and version control via GitHub. This experience strengthened my skills in robotics, teamwork, and real-world engineering. Being part of a high-performing team taught me how to rapidly iterate designs, debug complex systems, and stay adaptable under competitive pressure—essential skills I now bring to every technical challenge.

projects.title: Hydra
projects.summary: Custom CNC robot with dual slides and turret intake. Iterative design and coding let us compete at FTC’s first New England Premier event.
projects.description:
For the FTC Centerstage competition, I initially developed a pivot arm using the Studica drivetrain system, which allowed rapid prototyping and reliable performance during early matches. This setup helped our team quickly test core mechanisms and strategies.

Building on that, I designed and fabricated a fully custom aluminum arm assembly to improve precision and durability. The new design features a transfer mechanism that coordinates two arms—one fixed and one turret-mounted—allowing greater reach and versatility in scoring tasks. The turret arm can rotate independently, enabling complex manipulation without repositioning the whole robot. I engineered the system with lightweight aluminum for strength and speed, integrated precise motor controls, and optimized sensor feedback for autonomous operation. Additionally, I implemented Pedro Pathing with spline trajectories for the autonomous period, enabling the robot to follow smooth, optimal paths that maximize scoring efficiency. This custom arm and advanced pathing significantly enhanced our robot’s functionality and competitive edge throughout the season. My contributions in mechanical design, programming, and iterative testing were key to achieving reliable performance in regional competitions.

projects.title: BigFluffyRobot
projects.summary: A boxing robot on a Bracket Bot, driven from a web dashboard and posed by human moves seen through a camera.
projects.description: A hackathon project: a Bracket Bot that boxes. You can drive it from a web dashboard, and it copies human boxing moves seen by a laptop camera. Pose detection runs in the browser, and the Python server turns the moves into arm motion.

projects.title: Inkference
projects.summary: A portfolio and social app for builders. Show your work, chat live, plan your week, run a booth and join communities, all in one place.
projects.description:
Inkference is a portfolio and social platform for builders. Instead of a plain resume, you get a living profile that shows what you've built, what you know and what you're working on right now.

You can share posts, chat live with friends and groups, plan your week, keep notes, trackers and sheets in your own Drive, run a small side business from a booth, and join communities and enterprises. It works in the browser and installs on your phone like a normal app.

projects.title: Playlistify

projects.title: Xenon Economy (Discord Bot)
projects.summary: An engaging economy bot with trading, earning, events, mini-games & player battles — grew to 100 servers during the COVID pandemic.
projects.description:
I created a Discord economy bot during the COVID pandemic that quickly grew to over 100 servers and a community of 800+ users. The bot featured an engaging economy system where players could trade items, earn virtual currency through various activities, and participate in dynamic events that granted money and rare items. Users could also interact with one another via features like fighting duels and mini-games, which made the experience fun and interactive.

Throughout this project, I learned and adapted to many technologies, including MongoDB for managing the database, Heroku for hosting the bot, and the Discord.js library to interface with Discord’s API. Keeping up with Discord.js’s frequent updates was challenging but rewarding. I also built and nurtured a growing community around the bot within the Discord server itself.

Unfortunately, when Heroku discontinued its free hosting plan and I was unable to verify the bot, it went out of service, which was disappointing. However, this was an incredible learning journey for me, and I’m proud of how far the bot and community grew. It was a cool project, and I don’t plan to improve or continue it — it’s done, but definitely a great experience.

projects.title: Dank Exclusive (Discord Bot)
projects.summary: Created Dank Exclusive bot during COVID to boost server activity with leveling, automated events, booster perks, moderation, and automod features.
projects.description:
During the COVID pandemic, I helped build the Dank Exclusive Discord bot to enhance server engagement and management. The main goal was to encourage activity by implementing a leveling system that rewarded users for participation, helping to keep the community lively during a difficult time. The bot automated event creation and hosting, making it easier for moderators to run giveaways, contests, and special server happenings without manual effort.

One key feature was automating perks for server boosters—those who support the server financially—by granting exclusive rewards and benefits automatically, which helped maintain ongoing server funding and kept boosters appreciated. Additionally, Dank Exclusive handled moderation tasks, including automoderation tools that filtered spam and enforced rules, helping maintain a positive and safe environment for all members.

This project deepened my understanding of bot development, server management, and how to balance automation with community interaction. It was rewarding to see how automation reduced the moderators’ workload and increased member participation. Overall, Dank Exclusive was a meaningful and practical bot that greatly improved the server experience during the pandemic.

projects.title: Personal Website V1
projects.summary: Personal portfolio site built with ReactJS, showcasing improved skills in routing, components, and state management.
projects.description: This website was created as a portfolio to share my life. Although I previously struggled with ReactJS and relied on YouTube tutorials, I've now gained a better understanding of web development. I revisited ReactJS to build something new, learning to organize the website into different pages with components, implement routing, and use ReactJS functions like "useEffect()" and "useState()". While this website doesn't fully utilize ReactJS's capabilities, I plan to work on a future project, such as a social media or communications site, incorporating features like login/signup, live messaging, posts, and basic encryption security. I am also looking to learn how to use Google's Firebase for website hosting and integrate my database knowledge with MongoDB and Cloudinary for storing media files.

projects.title: Noutes V1
projects.summary: PHP site with session-based login/signup, note creation, and a car shop with cart, live pricing, and lazy-loaded images for smoother performance.
projects.description: The purpose of creating this website was to learn how to implement PHP in web development. The website uses PHP's session storage to provide a fully functional signup and login mechanism. Users can create accounts, and their activities are saved in the session storage. When logged in, users can create notes with a title, description, and image. The website also features a car shop, demonstrating simple e-commerce functionality, including adding cars to a cart, clearing the cart, and live total price updates. Cars in the shop are represented by objects with images, prices, and descriptions to inform users about the details. Additionally, I learned how to implement lazy loading for images that take longer to load.

projects.title: Story of Star Boy RPG
projects.summary: 2D Pygame catcher game with star collection, fuel/HP systems, boss battles, shooting, and an RPG-style storyline.
projects.description: I created a 2D catcher game using Pygame for my grade 11 computer science course submission. This game incorporated all the basics of Python programming taught throughout the year. It features the dropping and collection of stars, a fuel management system, an HP management system for both the player and bosses, and a mechanic allowing the player to shoot light pulses to defeat bosses. Additionally, a short storyline was included to enhance the game with RPG elements.
